mechaber.he: האיש שסילק עצמו מפירות נכסי אשתו ומירושתה. ובו ח סעיפים: הכותב או האומר לאשתו בעודה ארוסה דין ודברים אין לי בנכסיך אם מכרה או נתנה קיים ואין לו במעות המקח כלל (הגהות אלפסי) וכל זמן שלא מכרה ולא נתנה הבעל אוכל הפירות ואם מתה יורשה ואם כתב לה כן אחר הנישואין צריך לקנות מידו ואז יהיה מכרה ומתנתה קיים: הגה ולא מהני סלוקו אלא לאחר אירוסין אבל קודם אירוסין לא מהני סילוק (ר"ן ריש פ' הכותב ורשב"א סי' תתק"ס):
mechaber.en: The man who removed himself from produce of his wife's property and from her inheritance. It contains 8 seifim. One who writes or says to his wife while she is betrothed "I have no claim or right in your property" — if she sells or gives, it stands; and he has nothing at all in the sale money (Hagahot Alfasi). And as long as she did not sell and did not give — the husband eats the produce, and if she dies he inherits her. And if he wrote for her thus after marriage — they must acquire from his hand, and then her sale and gift stand. {Rama: And his removal is effective only after betrothal; but before betrothal removal does not help (Ran beginning of HaKotev and Rashba siman 465).}

mechaber.he: אם התנה בעודה ארוסה על נכסים שיפלו לה משנשאת שלא יהא לו דין ודברים בהם מועיל ויש מי שאומר שאינו מועיל: הגה סלק עצמו מנכסים י"א שאין הנכסים הכתובים בכתובה בכלל (מרדכי פ' הכותב בשם ריצב"א) (ואפי' נכסים שנפלו לה אח"כ אינו בכלל) (מהרי"ק שורש י"ג) אא"כ פי' בהדיא:
mechaber.en:
If he stipulated while she was betrothed regarding property that will fall to her from when she marries that he will have no claim or right in them — it is effective. And some say it is not effective.

mechaber.en:
He stipulated with her that he not inherit her — he does not inherit her but eats produce during her lifetime. And likewise if he stipulated with her that if she dies without children the property returns to her father's house — all stands. When does this apply? When he stipulated with her before she marries while she is betrothed, or when writing for her in her ketubah at the time of entry. But if he stipulated with her after she married — his stipulation is void and he inherits her.

{Rama: And see above siman 69. And that a stipulation after she married is not effective is specifically when he said he will not inherit her; nevertheless if he obligated himself to return to her heirs what he inherits from her — he must fulfill (Ran beginning of HaKotev in name of Ramban and Rivash simanim 64 and 102).}
